titleEn: Trauma Systems and Mechanism of Injury
whyEn: Exam weight 2/3. This chapter is the reasoning layer that runs before every other trauma chapter: it trains you to read a vehicle, a weapon, a fall, or a blast scene and predict hidden injury before the physical exam confirms it. It carries fewer drug-dose numbers than the shock or airway chapters, but it is where BC's 'automatically unstable' mechanism-of-injury cut-offs live — free-fall height, vehicle intrusion, pedestrian and motorcycle impact speed — and those exact numbers are directly testable on both the written and practical exam.
whyZh: 考试权重 2/3。这一章是所有其他创伤章节前面的推理层：训练你看一眼车、看一眼凶器、看一眼坠落高度或爆炸现场，就能在体查证实之前先预测出隐藏损伤。它的药物剂量数字比休克或气道章少，但 BC「自动判不稳定」的受伤机制切点——坠落高度、车厢侵入量、行人/摩托车撞击速度——全部住在这一章，而且这些具体数字在笔试和实操考里都会被直接考。

points.en: Trauma is defined as a transfer of energy applied clinically, and it is the leading cause of death in Canadians younger than 34 — unintentional trauma is often called the 'silent epidemic' because roughly 90% of it is preventable.
points.zh: 创伤的定义是临床意义上的能量转移，也是加拿大 34 岁以下人群的头号死因——非故意创伤常被称为「沉默的流行病」，因为约 90% 都是可以预防的。

points.en: Scale of the problem in Canada: unintentional injuries cause more than 13,000 deaths a year (the third-leading cause of death overall), over 260,000 hospital admissions a year, and about $20 billion in direct and indirect costs.
points.zh: 加拿大的规模：非故意伤害每年造成超过 13,000 人死亡（总死因排名第三），每年超过 260,000 例住院，直接加间接成本约 200 亿加元。

points.en: The top five causes of trauma death are motor vehicle collisions, falls, poisonings, burns, and drownings.
points.zh: 创伤死亡的五大原因：机动车碰撞、跌落、中毒、烧伤、溺水。

points.en: You are the eyes and ears of the emergency department at the scene: your written and verbal mechanism-of-injury (MOI) report is often the physicians' only window into forces that produced injuries the exam has not yet revealed. Learning kinetics lets you predict those injuries before the exam proves them.
points.zh: 你是急诊团队在现场的眼睛和耳朵：你写的和说的受伤机制（MOI）报告，往往是医生了解「造成了体查还没查出来的损伤的那股力量」的唯一窗口。学会运动学，就能在体查证实之前先预测这些损伤。

sections.titleEn: Energy, Biomechanics, and What Determines Injury Severity
sections.titleZh: 能量、生物力学与损伤严重度的决定因素

points.en: Trauma physically means the body's tissues are exposed to external energy that dissipates faster than the body can absorb or disperse it. Five external energy sources: mechanical (kinetic = motion; potential = stored, e.g. gravity in a fall), chemical (explosives, acids, ingested or delivered agents), thermal, electrical (high-voltage shock, lightning), and barometric (rapid pressure change — diving, flying).
points.zh: 创伤的物理定义：身体组织暴露在外部能量下，而这股能量释放的速度超过身体吸收/消散的能力。五种外部能量来源：机械能（动能=运动中；势能=储存的，例如坠落时的重力）、化学能（爆炸物、酸、摄入或注射的药物）、热能、电能（高压电击、雷击）、气压能（快速压力变化——潜水、飞行）。

points.en: Biomechanics is the physiology-plus-mechanical-engineering study of injury; kinetics studies the relationship among speed, mass, force direction, and the resulting physical injury — this is the tool that lets you predict injury patterns before the exam confirms them.
points.zh: 生物力学＝用机械工程的方法研究损伤的生理学；运动学研究速度、质量、力的方向和实际损伤之间的关系——这是让你在体查证实之前先预测损伤模式的工具。

points.en: Injury severity is driven by the real-world version of Newton's second law (force = mass x acceleration): the mass/size of the object, its velocity, its acceleration or deceleration, the body area struck, and the duration and rate at which the force is applied.
points.zh: 损伤严重度由牛顿第二定律（力＝质量×加速度）的现实版本决定：物体的质量/大小、速度、加速或减速、受力的身体部位，以及施力的持续时间和速率。

points.en: Rate of application matters as much as total energy: the same energy delivered rapidly can break a wrist, while delivered slowly over time it may only produce a repetitive-stress injury.
points.zh: 施力速率和总能量一样重要：同样大小的能量，快速施加可能打断手腕，慢慢长期施加则可能只造成重复性劳损。

points.en: The larger the area over which force is dissipated, the lower the pressure at any single point — the defining feature of blunt trauma, which is why severe internal injury can hide behind almost no external marking (the same principle by which a ballistic vest's ceramic plate spreads a bullet's energy over a wide area).
points.zh: 力量分散的面积越大，任一点承受的压强就越低——这正是钝性伤的特征，所以严重内伤常常藏在几乎看不出外伤的表皮之下（防弹背心的陶瓷板把子弹能量分散到大面积，也是同一个原理）。

points.en: At the Scene: a cracked windshield, a deformed steering wheel or dashboard, vehicle intrusion, or fractured feet/ankles after a fall should all raise suspicion for spinal injury and change how you run the primary survey.
points.zh: 现场提示：挡风玻璃裂、方向盘或仪表板变形、车厢侵入、或坠落后出现足/踝骨折，都应该提高对脊柱损伤的怀疑，并改变你处理初次评估的方式。

sections.titleEn: Kinetics: Velocity, Kinetic Energy, and Newton's Laws
sections.titleZh: 运动学：速度、动能与牛顿定律

points.en: Velocity is distance per unit time in a specific direction (unlike speed); acceleration is the rate of change of velocity; gravity (g) accelerates any falling object downward at 9.8 m/sec2.
points.zh: 速度是单位时间内沿特定方向移动的距离（与速率不同）；加速度是速度的变化率；重力（g）使任何下落物体以 9.8 m/sec2 向下加速。

points.en: Kinetic energy (KE) = 1/2 x mass x velocity^2 — velocity dominates severity far more than mass because it is squared: doubling an object's speed quadruples its KE, while doubling its weight only doubles it.
points.zh: 动能（KE）＝½×质量×速度²——速度对严重度的影响远大于质量，因为它是平方项：速度翻倍，动能变成 4 倍；质量翻倍，动能只变成 2 倍。

points.en: Worked KE comparison for a person: at 70 kg, 55 km/h gives about 211,750 KE units and 65 km/h gives about 295,750 — just 10 km/h more speed adds roughly 84,000 KE units, dwarfing the effect of adding 10 kg of body weight at the same speed.
points.zh: 70 kg 的人举例：55 km/h 时动能约 211,750 单位，65 km/h 时约 295,750 单位——仅仅多 10 km/h 的速度就多出约 84,000 个动能单位，远大于同速度下多背 10 kg 体重的影响。

points.en: Law of conservation of energy: energy is neither created nor destroyed, only converted between thermal, electrical, chemical, radiant, and mechanical forms — braking slowly converts a vehicle's KE into heat via friction; a crash converts it into mechanical deformation of the car body instead.
points.zh: 能量守恒定律：能量不会凭空产生或消失，只会在热能、电能、化学能、辐射能和机械能之间转换——缓慢刹车把车的动能靠摩擦转成热能；撞车则把它转成车身的机械形变。

points.en: Newton's first law explains the unrestrained occupant: a body in motion stays in motion at constant velocity until acted on by an outside force, so when the vehicle stops abruptly, an unbelted occupant keeps travelling at the pre-crash speed until something else stops them.
points.zh: 牛顿第一定律解释了未系安全带的乘员：运动中的物体在受到外力前会一直保持匀速运动——所以车突然停下时，没系安全带的乘员会继续以撞车前的速度运动，直到被别的东西挡住。

points.en: Human deceleration tolerance tops out at about 30 g; high-speed collisions can generate deceleration forces in the hundreds of g — a 2-3 g deceleration already feels like being two or three times your normal weight.
points.zh: 人体能耐受的减速极限约 30 g；高速碰撞能产生数百 g 的减速力——2-3 g 的减速就已经让人感觉体重变成平时的两三倍。

points.en: Closing-speed rule: in a head-on collision the transferred energy is roughly the sum of both vehicles' speeds; in a rear impact travelling the same direction it is only the difference between their speeds (the closing speed) — which is why rear-end collisions are generally survived better than head-on ones at similar speeds.
points.zh: 相对速度规则：对头碰撞传递的能量大致是两车速度之和；同向行驶的追尾碰撞传递的能量只是两车的速度差（相对速度）——这就是为什么类似车速下追尾的生还率通常比对头碰撞高。

points.en: Multisystem trauma means two or more body systems are injured together (e.g. head plus spine, chest plus abdomen, chest plus extremities); the body compensates far worse for combined injuries than for one isolated injury.
points.zh: 多系统创伤指两个或以上身体系统同时受伤（例如头＋脊柱、胸＋腹、胸＋肢体）；身体对合并损伤的代偿能力，远不如对单一孤立损伤那么好。

points.en: It is usually produced by high-energy events (motor vehicle collisions, falls from height), often mixes blunt and penetrating mechanisms, and carries high morbidity and mortality — assess the entire body, prioritize the injuries found, and transport without delay.
points.zh: 通常由高能量事件造成（机动车碰撞、高处坠落），常常混合钝性和穿透性机制，致残致死率都高——要评估全身、给发现的损伤排优先级，并且不要拖延转运。

sections.titleEn: Blunt Trauma Fundamentals: Deceleration and Compression
sections.titleZh: 钝性伤基础：减速伤与压缩伤

points.en: Blunt trauma leaves tissue unpenetrated by an external object and is typical of MVCs, pedestrian strikes, motorcycle collisions, falls from height, serious sports injuries, and blasts with no shrapnel (pressure wave only). Penetrating trauma involves tissue disruption by one or more objects — gunshots, stabbings, and blasts with shrapnel — and can combine with blunt injury, such as an implement injury during an MVC.
points.zh: 钝性伤不穿透组织，典型见于机动车碰撞、行人被撞、摩托车事故、高处坠落、严重运动损伤，以及无弹片的爆炸（只有冲击波）。穿透伤是单个或多个物体造成的组织破坏——枪伤、刺伤、有弹片的爆炸——也可能和钝性伤合并出现，例如车祸中被车内器具刺伤。

points.en: Deceleration injury: a sudden stop of forward motion shears, avulses, or ruptures organs and their supporting fascia, vasculature, and nerves — these injuries are often invisible on exam, so suspicion must come from the mechanism itself.
points.zh: 减速伤：前向运动突然停止，会撕裂、撕脱或破坏器官及其支持筋膜、血管和神经——这类损伤常在体查中看不出来，怀疑度必须来自机制本身。

points.en: Head: the brain floats in fluid inside the skull, so any force that jerks the head causes the brain to strike the inside of the skull, producing bleeding, bruising, tearing, and crush injury — dangerous and easy to miss on a cursory exam.
points.zh: 头部：脑漂浮在颅内液体中，任何猛烈甩动头部的力都会让脑撞上颅骨内壁，造成出血、挫伤、撕裂和挤压伤——危险且粗略体查容易漏诊。

points.en: Chest: the aorta is the largest vessel in the body and the most common site of deceleration injury in the chest — it can shear away from its fixation points, causing rapid exsanguination and immediate death.
points.zh: 胸部：主动脉是全身最大血管，也是胸部减速伤最常见的部位——它可能从固定点被撕开，造成迅速失血和当场死亡。

points.en: Abdomen deceleration: liver, kidneys, small and large intestine, pancreas, and spleen can tear at their points of attachment or shear internally; small bowel can tear near the fixed large bowel and cause free air; a torn spleen can produce LUQ pain plus life-threatening bleeding.
points.zh: 腹部减速伤：肝、肾、大小肠、胰腺和脾都可能在固定点撕裂或内部剪切；小肠可能在靠近固定的大肠处撕裂并造成腹腔游离气体；脾撕裂可表现为左上腹痛加危及生命的出血。

points.en: Compression injuries come from dashboards, windshields, floors, and heavy falling objects: compression head injury often travels with cervical-spine injury (the worse the head injury, the more likely a C-spine injury too); chest compression fractures ribs, which can produce flail chest (a section of chest wall moving paradoxically) and blunt cardiac injury (arrhythmia, direct myocardial damage); abdominal compression against a seat belt can rupture bowel or bladder; pelvic fracture from compression can injure the bladder, vagina, rectum, and lumbar plexus with life-threatening bleeding.
points.zh: 压缩伤来自仪表板、挡风玻璃、地板和坠落的重物：头部压缩伤常合并颈椎损伤（头伤越重，合并颈椎伤的可能性越高）；胸部压缩可致肋骨骨折，进一步造成连枷胸（一段胸壁反常运动）和钝性心脏损伤（心律失常、心肌直接损伤）；腹部被安全带压迫可致肠道或膀胱破裂；骨盆压缩性骨折可伤及膀胱、阴道、直肠和腰丛并危及生命地出血。

sections.titleEn: Motor Vehicle Collisions: The Five Phases and Impact Patterns
sections.titleZh: 机动车碰撞：五阶段与撞击模式

points.en: Five phases of collision trauma, in order: (1) deceleration of the vehicle, (2) deceleration of the occupant, (3) deceleration of internal organs (fixed structures like skull/sternum/ribs/spine/pelvis stop first, movable organs like brain/heart/liver/spleen/kidneys/intestines keep moving until anatomic restraints stop them), (4) secondary impacts (loose objects, other passengers, or animals strike the occupant), (5) additional impacts (the vehicle itself is hit again and deflected).
points.zh: 碰撞创伤的五个阶段（按顺序）：①车辆减速 ②乘员减速 ③内脏器官减速（颅骨/胸骨/肋骨/脊柱/骨盆等固定结构先停，脑/心/肝/脾/肾/肠等可移动器官会继续运动直到被解剖学限制挡住）④二次撞击（车内松动物品、其他乘客或动物撞上乘员）⑤附加撞击（车辆再次被撞并偏转）。

points.en: Five impact patterns: frontal/head-on, lateral/side, rear, rotational/quarter-panel, and rollover.
points.zh: 五种撞击模式：正面/对头、侧面、追尾、旋转/斜角、翻滚。

points.en: Frontal rule of thumb: roughly 1.5 cm of front-end deformity per 1 km/h of speed — the book's worked example is about 60 cm of crush at 45 km/h. Unrestrained occupants follow one of two trajectories: down-and-under (knees lead into the dash, energy travels up the femur to the pelvis — locked feet risk midshaft femur fracture or hip dislocation) or up-and-over (head leads, striking windshield/roof/mirror/dash, producing head and cervical-spine trauma; the anterior neck can strike the wheel and fracture the larynx).
points.zh: 正面碰撞经验值：车速每 1 km/h 对应约 1.5 cm 前端变形——书中举例是 45 km/h 时约压缩 60 cm。未系安全带的乘员走两条轨迹之一：下潜路径（膝盖先撞仪表板，能量沿股骨传到骨盆——双脚被卡住时易致股骨干骨折或髋关节脱位）或上跃路径（头先撞挡风玻璃/车顶/后视镜/仪表板，造成头部和颈椎创伤；颈前部可能撞上方向盘导致喉部骨折）。

points.en: Paper-bag syndrome: the occupant reflexively takes a deep breath just before impact, closing the glottis and hyperinflating the lungs; the steering wheel then strikes the chest and the trapped pressure pops alveoli, producing a pneumothorax — an estimated 60% to 70% of steering-wheel-related pneumothoraces occur this way.
points.zh: 「纸袋综合征」：乘员在撞击前反射性深吸气、声门关闭、肺过度充气；方向盘撞击胸部时，困住的压力把肺泡撑破形成气胸——约 60%-70% 的方向盘相关气胸是这样产生的。

points.en: Lateral/T-bone impact: energy transfers almost directly into the near-side occupant's pelvis and chest; seat belts (designed for forward motion) protect poorly here; the shoulder rotates outward and up, exposing the chest and ribs to rib fractures, lateral flail chest, lung contusion, and diaphragm rupture. A restrained far-side occupant 'rides down' with the car (less force); an unrestrained one can collide with the near-side occupant, adding injury to both.
points.zh: 侧面/T形碰撞：能量几乎直接传入近侧乘员的骨盆和胸部；安全带（为前向运动设计）在这种碰撞里保护有限；肩部向外向上旋转，暴露胸部和肋骨，导致肋骨骨折、侧向连枷胸、肺挫伤和膈肌破裂。系了安全带的远侧乘员会随车「减速缓冲」（受力较小）；未系的则可能和近侧乘员相撞，两人都会因此加重损伤。

points.en: Lateral pelvic injury: force through the greater trochanter can drive into the acetabulum or ilium, producing a lateral-compression pelvic ring injury — generally less severe than anterior compression, and death in lateral collisions is usually from associated torso or head injury rather than the pelvis itself.
points.zh: 侧向骨盆损伤：经股骨大转子传入的力可能作用到髋臼或髂骨，造成侧方压缩型骨盆环损伤——通常比前方压缩伤轻，侧面碰撞的死亡多来自合并的躯干或头部损伤，而不是骨盆本身。

points.en: Rear impact: the neck hyperextends unless the headrest is correctly positioned; a headrest set too low acts as a fulcrum and worsens the extension injury, and seat elasticity can rebound the motion into flexion then a further extension — this whiplash sequence injures neck soft tissue and spine.
points.zh: 追尾碰撞：除非头枕位置正确，否则颈部会过伸；头枕太低会变成支点、加重过伸损伤，座椅的弹性还会把动作反弹成屈曲、再一次过伸——这一连串鞭甩动作会损伤颈部软组织和脊柱。

points.en: Rotational/quarter-panel impact: an off-centre hit stops part of the car while the rest rotates around the impact point; the site of greatest speed loss is where the worst patient injury occurs, and occupants typically show a combined frontal-plus-lateral injury pattern. Three-point belts remain effective in angled collisions up to 45 degrees.
points.zh: 旋转/斜角碰撞：偏心撞击让车的一部分停下，其余部分绕撞击点旋转；车速损失最大的位置，就是病人损伤最重的位置；乘员通常同时出现正面＋侧面的合并损伤模式。三点式安全带在最多 45° 的角度碰撞中仍然有效。

points.en: Rollover carries the greatest lethal potential even with seat belts worn; each direction change re-strikes the occupant, and an unbelted occupant may be ejected with each roll.
points.zh: 翻滚碰撞即使系了安全带也有最高的致命潜力；车每变一次方向，乘员就会被再撞一次，没系安全带的乘员可能随每一次翻滚被甩出车外。

points.en: Ejection statistics: being ejected raises the risk of death by 2 to 25 times; one of every three ejected victims sustains a cervical-spine fracture, and one of every 13 sustains major, permanent cervical-spine damage.
points.zh: 抛出统计：被甩出车外会使死亡风险升高 2-25 倍；每 3 名被甩出者中就有 1 人发生颈椎骨折，每 13 人中就有 1 人留下重大永久性颈椎损伤。

sections.titleEn: Restraints, Trauma Scoring, and Special Populations
sections.titleZh: 约束装置、创伤评分与特殊人群

points.en: Restrained occupants 'ride down' the crash with belt elasticity and crush time, producing nearly a 45% reduction in fatalities; seat belt use alone is associated with a 33% reduction in all injuries and more than a 50% reduction in major injuries.
points.zh: 系安全带的乘员能靠带子弹性和车身溃缩时间「缓冲减速」，使死亡率降低近 45%；单是系安全带就能让全部损伤减少 33%，重大损伤减少超过 50%。

points.en: A belt worn across the abdomen instead of low across the pelvis allows abdominal and lumbar-spine injury; belt-specific injuries also include cervical flexion fractures and hyperextension neck sprain.
points.zh: 安全带如果压在腹部而不是压低在骨盆上，会导致腹部和腰椎损伤；与安全带相关的特有损伤还包括颈椎屈曲骨折和过伸性颈部扭伤。

points.en: Air bags reduce deaths in direct frontal collisions by about 30%, but are single-use (no protection in a second impact), may not deploy for side or quarter-panel impacts, and can themselves cause facial/chest/arm abrasions and burns, chemical keratitis or conjunctivitis, corneal abrasion, and inhalation injury; a deployed front air bag can severely injure or kill a small child riding in the front seat.
points.zh: 安全气囊能让正面碰撞死亡率降低约 30%，但只能用一次（对二次撞击无保护）、侧面或斜角碰撞时可能不会弹出，而且本身可能造成面部/胸部/手臂擦伤和烧伤、化学性角膜炎或结膜炎、角膜擦伤和吸入伤；坐前排的小孩若遇气囊弹出，可能被严重伤害甚至致命。

points.en: Trauma Score (1-16, 16 best) combines GCS, respiratory rate, respiratory expansion, systolic BP, and capillary refill, but does not reliably predict survival in severe isolated head injury because motor and verbal deficits confound it — the Revised Trauma Score (RTS, 0-12, 12 best; built from GCS, SBP, and respiratory rate) is used instead in that situation.
points.zh: 创伤评分（Trauma Score，1-16 分，16 分最好）综合 GCS、呼吸频率、呼吸幅度、收缩压和毛细血管再充盈，但对严重孤立性头外伤的生存预测不可靠，因为运动和语言反应会被头伤本身干扰——这种情况改用改良创伤评分（RTS，0-12 分，12 分最好；由 GCS、收缩压和呼吸频率构成）。

points.en: Geriatric patients: simple ground-level falls can produce serious chest, pelvis, hip, spine, and head injury; more brittle bones raise the risk of rib and sternal fractures, which can progress to lung contusion and respiratory compromise; age-related changes in vision, hearing, posture, and motor ability also raise pedestrian-strike risk.
points.zh: 老年病人：简单的平地跌倒也可能造成严重的胸、盆、髋、脊柱和头部损伤；骨骼更脆使肋骨和胸骨骨折风险更高，可能进一步发展成肺挫伤和呼吸功能受损；视力、听力、姿势和运动能力的年龄性改变，也会提高被车撞的风险。

points.en: Pediatric patients: a child who has outgrown a car seat but is too small for an adult belt (no booster) risks hyperflexion and abdominal injury; properly used child restraints cut fatalities by 25%; children mostly sustain blunt head injury because the head is proportionally larger and penetrating injury is uncommon in childhood, though a severe whole-body mechanism can still produce a head-chest-abdomen-long-bone pattern.
points.zh: 儿童病人：已经坐不下儿童安全座椅、但还不够格用成人安全带（没用增高垫）的孩子，容易发生过屈和腹部损伤；正确使用儿童约束装置能让死亡率降低 25%；因为儿童头部相对身体更大且穿透伤少见，儿童多为头部钝性伤，但严重的全身性机制仍可能造成头＋胸＋腹＋长骨的合并损伤模式。

points.en: Pregnancy: proper lap-plus-shoulder belt use decreases both maternal and fetal injury (the myth that belts worsen fetal injury is unfounded); a lap belt worn alone and too high allows forward flexion that can rupture the uterus, and steering-wheel or dashboard injury sustained because a belt was not worn, or worn incorrectly, carries a 50% fetal death rate.
points.zh: 孕妇：正确使用「腰带＋肩带」组合能同时降低母体和胎儿损伤（安全带会加重胎儿损伤是没有依据的迷思）；只系腰带且系得太高，会让身体前屈压迫子宫甚至致其破裂；因未系或系错安全带而受到方向盘或仪表板撞击，胎儿死亡率高达 50%。

points.en: Patients on anticoagulants are at increased risk of severe bleeding, and even a minor, initially asymptomatic head injury can turn catastrophic — always ask about anticoagulant medications and ensure timely hospital assessment.
points.zh: 服用抗凝药的病人失血风险更高，即使是当下无症状的轻微头外伤也可能演变成灾难性后果——一定要问抗凝药物史，并确保病人得到及时的医院评估。

points.en: In Canada (2016), motorcycles made up only 2.8% of licensed vehicles but accounted for 10.9% of road-user fatalities; motorcycling deaths more than doubled in the 45-54 age group over the preceding decade as ownership grew in that group.
points.zh: 在加拿大（2016 年），摩托车只占领牌车辆的 2.8%，却占道路使用者死亡数的 10.9%；随着这一年龄段的车主增多，45-54 岁人群的摩托车死亡人数在过去十年翻了一倍多。

points.en: Rider protection comes from gear, not a steel cage: a helmet protects against direct head-impact forces but transmits that impact into the cervical spine, so it does NOT protect against severe cervical injury; leather/synthetic gear protects mainly against road abrasion, not blunt trauma from secondary impacts.
points.zh: 骑手的防护来自装备而不是钢制车身：头盔能防头部直接撞击力，但会把冲击力传入颈椎，所以并不能防止严重颈椎损伤；皮衣/合成材料装备主要防路面摩擦伤，对二次撞击的钝性伤没有防护作用。

points.en: Scene clues at a motorcycle collision: deformity of the motorcycle, side of most damage, skid distance, deformity of the struck object or vehicle, extent and location of helmet deformity, and the distance of the patient from the vehicle or object.
points.zh: 摩托车事故现场线索：摩托车的变形程度、损伤最重的一侧、刹车痕迹长度、被撞物体或车辆的变形、头盔变形的部位和程度，以及病人与车辆/物体之间的距离。

points.en: Four motorcycle impact types: head-on (rider pitches over the handlebars; feet locked on pegs risks bilateral femur/tibia fracture, and low-riding 'wedge' bikes drive the tank into the pelvis, causing severe anterior-posterior pelvic compression and open pelvic fracture with mortality approaching 50%); angular (crushing lower-extremity injury between bike and object, often needing surgical amputation, plus torso torsion/spine injury if the rider is thrown over the colliding vehicle); ejection (high-speed road rash from drag plus unpredictable secondary blunt injury); laying the bike down (a controlled-separation technique that, if properly geared, limits injury to abrasion and any secondary impact — but a rider who cannot clear the bike hits the object with devastating results).
points.zh: 四种摩托车撞击类型：正面（骑手被甩过车把；双脚卡在踏板上易致双侧股骨/胫骨骨折，低坐垫「楔形」车型会让油箱楔入骨盆造成严重前后方向骨盆压缩伤和开放性骨盆骨折，死亡率可接近 50%）；角度撞击（下肢被挤压在车与物体之间，常需外科截肢，若骑手被甩过对方车辆还可能合并躯干扭转/脊柱损伤）；被甩出（高速拖擦造成道路擦伤，加上不可预测的二次钝性伤）；「放倒车」技巧（受控分离技术，装备齐全时能把损伤限制在擦伤和可能的二次撞击——但来不及脱离车身的骑手会直接撞上物体，后果严重）。

points.en: Bicycles and off-road vehicles (four-wheelers, snowmobiles) produce similar injuries to motorcycles, but riders often lack helmets or protective gear, and remote crash locations can make access and evacuation the biggest challenge; cyclists struck by a vehicle sustain injury patterns similar to struck pedestrians.
points.zh: 自行车和越野车（四轮沙滩车、雪地摩托）造成的损伤和摩托车类似，但骑手常常没有头盔或防护装备，而且事故地点偏远时，到达和撤离本身就是最大的挑战；被车撞的骑自行车者，其损伤模式和被撞行人类似。

points.en: Any motorcycle or off-road collision should be treated with C-spine precaution; helmet removal can be done by cutting and removing it, or leaving it in place if removal would introduce further neck deformation.
points.zh: 任何摩托车或越野车事故都应按颈椎防护处理；头盔可以剪开摘除，如果摘除会造成颈部进一步变形，则应保留在原位。

points.en: Canada (2016): nearly 350 pedestrians killed and about 10,000 injured; adults over 65 accounted for 35% of pedestrian fatalities despite being only 13% of the population; 60% of pedestrians killed were crossing the road and 40% had been drinking. In 2011, 67 cyclists were killed in motor vehicle collisions.
points.zh: 加拿大（2016 年）：近 350 名行人死亡、约 10,000 人受伤；65 岁以上成人占行人死亡数的 35%，而他们只占人口的 13%；60% 被撞身亡的行人当时正在过马路，40% 曾饮酒。2011 年有 67 名骑车人死于机动车碰撞。

points.en: More than 85% of pedestrians are struck by the vehicle's front end. Adults tend to turn to the side or away from impact (lateral/posterior injury pattern), while children may face forward into traffic.
points.zh: 超过 85% 的行人被车辆前端撞击。成人被撞时习惯侧身或转身避让（侧方/后方损伤模式），儿童则可能正面朝向来车。

points.en: Adult three-impact sequence: (1) the bumper strikes the lower extremity, typically fracturing tibia/fibula (often with open knee dislocation or tibial plateau fracture, usually on the impact side); (2) the body is thrown onto the hood/grille, causing head, pelvis, and chest injury plus coup-contrecoup traumatic brain injury (lateral-compression pelvic fracture is common here); (3) the body strikes the ground or another object after being thrown.
points.zh: 成人的三次撞击顺序：①保险杠先撞下肢，通常造成胫腓骨骨折（常合并开放性膝关节脱位或胫骨平台骨折，多发生在撞击侧）②身体被抛上引擎盖/格栅，造成头、盆、胸损伤加对冲性脑外伤（这一步常见侧方压缩型骨盆骨折）③身体被抛出后落地或撞上其他物体。

points.en: Field rule: a dislocated knee should be splinted in the position found if distal pulse/motor/sensation (PMS) is intact; if the knee spontaneously reduces, you MUST report this verbally and in writing to the trauma team — spontaneous reduction is a sign of possible vascular injury that the team could otherwise miss.
points.zh: 现场原则：如果远端脉搏/运动/感觉（PMS）完好，脱位的膝关节应按发现时的姿势固定；如果膝关节自行复位，必须口头加书面向创伤团队报告——自行复位提示可能存在血管损伤，不报告的话团队可能会漏诊。

points.en: Waddell triad describes the injury pattern in children and short-statured pedestrians: (1) the bumper hits the pelvis and femurs instead of the knees/tibias, (2) the chest and abdomen hit the grille or low on the hood (sternal/rib fracture), (3) the head strikes the vehicle then the ground (skull/facial fracture, closed head injury). Children are less likely than adults to fly over the hood and more likely to be run over.
points.zh: Waddell 三联征描述儿童和身材矮小行人的损伤模式：①保险杠撞在骨盆和股骨而不是膝盖/胫骨 ②胸腹撞在格栅或引擎盖低处（胸骨/肋骨骨折）③头先撞车再撞地（颅骨/面部骨折、闭合性颅脑损伤）。儿童比成人更不容易被抛上引擎盖，反而更容易被车辆碾压。

points.en: High-risk fall groups: children under 5 near a window or porch higher than 3 m with inadequate railings; adult falls from height are often linked to criminal activity, suicide attempts, or intoxication.
points.zh: 高危坠落人群：5 岁以下、靠近高于 3 m 且护栏不足的窗户或阳台的儿童；成人高处坠落常与犯罪活动、自杀企图或醉酒/中毒有关。

points.en: Fall physics: a falling body accelerates at 9.8 m/sec2, so a 2-second fall reaches an impact velocity of nearly 20 m/sec.
points.zh: 坠落物理：下落物体以 9.8 m/sec2 加速，坠落 2 秒时的撞击速度接近 20 m/sec。

points.en: Height/force examples: a fall of one storey (3.5 m) onto concrete produces an impact velocity of about 9 m/sec and roughly 48 g of force; a fall from the second storey (8 m) reaches about 14 m/sec and roughly 95 g. Using 3.5 m per storey, a fall of about 4 storeys (~14 m) kills roughly 50% of fallers, and about 7 storeys (~24.5 m) kills roughly 90%.
points.zh: 高度/冲击力示例：从一层楼高（3.5 m）摔到混凝土上，撞击速度约 9 m/sec、冲击力约 48 g；从二层楼高（8 m）摔下，速度约 14 m/sec、冲击力约 95 g。按每层 3.5 m 换算，约 4 层楼高（约 14 m）的坠落会导致约 50% 的坠落者死亡，约 7 层楼高（约 24.5 m）会导致约 90% 死亡。

points.en: Body position at impact shapes the injury pattern: children tend to fall head-first (proportionally heavier head), producing head injury plus wrist/upper-extremity injury from an outstretched-arm attempt to break the fall. Adults tend to land feet-first, producing the Don Juan syndrome (lover's-leap) pattern — foot and lower-extremity fracture, hip/acetabular/pelvic-ring/sacral fracture, lumbar axial-load compression or burst fracture (especially T12-L1 and L2), vertical-deceleration organ injury (liver, spleen, aorta), and forearm/wrist fracture.
points.zh: 落地瞬间的体位决定损伤模式：儿童常头先落地（头部相对更重），造成头部损伤加因伸手撑地而来的腕/上肢损伤。成人常脚先落地，形成「唐璜综合征」（跳崖者模式）——足和下肢骨折、髋/髋臼/骨盆环/骶骨骨折、腰椎轴向负荷压缩或爆裂骨折（尤其 T12-L1 和 L2）、垂直减速造成的器官损伤（肝、脾、主动脉）和前臂/腕骨折。

points.en: Other severity modifiers: a larger contact area dissipates force over more surface (lower peak pressure); surface plasticity matters (deep snow deforms well, but concrete — and, counterintuitively, water at high speed — has almost no plasticity); surface hazards like a picket fence are more dangerous than plain grass; and pre-existing conditions matter — osteoporosis predisposes to fracture from a minimal fall, an enlarged spleen predisposes to rupture, and children under 3 tend to have fewer injuries from falls over 3 storeys than older children or adults because of more elastic tissue and less ossification.
points.zh: 其他影响严重度的因素：接触面积越大，力量分散得越开（峰值压强越低）；地面的可塑性也重要（厚雪能很好地形变，但混凝土——反直觉的是高速撞击下的水——几乎没有可塑性）；带尖刺的栅栏等地面障碍物比平坦草地更危险；既往病史也影响——骨质疏松使轻微跌倒也能骨折，脾脏肿大者更容易脾破裂，而 3 岁以下儿童从超过 3 层楼高处坠落时受伤反而比年长儿童和成人少，因为组织更有弹性、骨化程度更低。

sections.titleEn: Penetrating Trauma: Stab and Gunshot Wounds

points.en: Penetrating trauma disrupts skin and tissue in a small, focused area, unlike blunt trauma's broad-area force. In Canada, firearms and stabbings are the most common sources; Canadian firearm deaths run about 1,000 a year, with 2-3 additional people injured per death: 80% of gun fatalities are suicides, 15% homicides, and 4% unintentional.
points.zh: 穿透伤把皮肤和组织的破坏集中在一个小范围，不像钝性伤那样力量分散在大面积。在加拿大，枪支和刺伤是最常见的穿透伤来源；加拿大每年约 1,000 例枪支死亡，每例死亡还伴随 2-3 人受伤：80% 的枪支死亡是自杀，15% 是他杀，4% 是意外。

points.en: Shooting and stabbing homicide rates in Canada run about equal (roughly 0.55 vs 0.56 deaths per 100,000 per year, 1996-2016), and guns are involved in about one-third of homicides. Canada's firearm homicide rate (0.5 per 100,000 in 2011) was about 7 times lower than the United States' (3.5 per 100,000).
points.zh: 在加拿大，枪杀和刺杀的他杀率大致相当（1996-2016 年约每 10 万人 0.55 例 vs 0.56 例），约三分之一的他杀涉及枪支。加拿大的枪支他杀率（2011 年每 10 万人 0.5 例）大约只有美国（每 10 万人 3.5 例）的七分之一。

points.en: Stab-wound severity depends on anatomic area, depth of penetration, blade length, and angle. Neck wounds risk the carotid/subclavian vessels, lung apex, mediastinum, trachea, esophagus, and thoracic duct — deep enough, they can injure the spinal cord and cervical spine. Lower-chest or upper-abdominal wounds may cross the diaphragm depending on whether the patient was inhaling or exhaling at the moment of injury, risking rapidly fatal cardiac, lung, or major-vessel injury.
points.zh: 刺伤严重度取决于解剖部位、刺入深度、刀刃长度和角度。颈部伤口可能伤及颈动脉/锁骨下血管、肺尖、纵隔、气管、食管和胸导管——足够深还可能伤及脊髓和颈椎。下胸或上腹部伤口能否穿过膈肌，取决于受伤当下病人是吸气还是呼气，可能造成迅速致命的心脏、肺或大血管损伤。

points.en: Documentation rule: never label a wound 'entry' or 'exit' — describe only the location, size, and shape of what you see, because your record may be used in criminal proceedings and mislabelling can mislead the investigation.
points.zh: 记录原则：绝不要把伤口标注为「入口」或「出口」——只描述你看到的位置、大小和形状，因为你的记录可能被用在刑事诉讼中，贴错标签可能误导调查。

points.en: Gunshot severity depends on firearm type (shotgun, rifle, or handgun), projectile velocity and design, muzzle-to-target distance, and the type of tissue struck. Shotguns fire multiple unspun pellets that disperse with distance (devastating under 10 m); rifles fire a single spin-stabilized high-velocity projectile through a rifled barrel; handguns (revolvers holding 6-10 rounds, pistols up to 17) are also rifled but shorter-barrelled, less accurate, and generally less powerful than rifles.
points.zh: 枪伤严重度取决于枪支类型（霰弹枪、步枪或手枪）、弹丸速度和设计、枪口到目标的距离，以及被击中的组织类型。霰弹枪发射多枚不带旋转的弹丸，距离越远散布越开（10 m 内威力极大）；步枪通过来复线膛管发射单枚高速旋转稳定的弹头；手枪（左轮 6-10 发，弹匣式最多 17 发）同样有膛线但枪管更短，精度和威力通常都不如步枪。

points.en: Tissue elasticity determines wound severity: elastic tissue (muscle, bowel, lung) tolerates temporary cavitation (stretch) better than inelastic tissue (liver, spleen, brain), where the temporary cavity can become a permanent defect — so a low-velocity bullet through the liver or aorta can do more damage than a high-velocity one through fleshy muscle.
points.zh: 组织弹性决定伤口严重度：有弹性的组织（肌肉、肠、肺）比没有弹性的组织（肝、脾、脑）更能承受暂时性空腔化（拉伸）——没有弹性的组织，暂时性空腔可能变成永久性缺损——所以低速子弹打穿肝脏或主动脉，可能比高速子弹打穿肌肉造成更大的损伤。

points.en: Wound mechanics: the permanent cavity is the direct crush path of the projectile (straight or deflected by bone); temporary cavitation ('pathway expansion') comes from sonic shock waves travelling about 4 times the speed of sound in air; missile fragmentation and secondary missiles (bone, teeth, clothing) create their own injury paths; exit wounds occur when residual energy remains and are usually irregular and larger than the entry wound, sometimes multiple if the projectile fragmented.
points.zh: 伤道力学：永久性空腔是弹丸直接压碎的路径（可能被骨头偏转）；暂时性空腔化（「路径扩张」）来自以约 4 倍空气中声速传播的声波冲击；弹丸碎裂和继发投射物（骨片、牙齿、衣物碎片）会形成自己的伤道；只要还有残余能量，弹丸就会造成出口伤，出口伤通常边缘不规则且比入口大，弹丸碎裂时甚至可能有多个出口。

points.en: Close-range signs: powder-burn tattooing around the wound at close range, muzzle-blast burns at extremely close range, and heavy wound contamination from negative pressure behind the travelling projectile sucking in clothing and debris — all raising infection risk.
points.zh: 近距离射击的迹象：近距离时伤口周围有火药烧灼纹身样痕迹，极近距离时有枪口爆炸烧伤，弹丸经过时在其后方形成负压把衣物碎屑吸入伤口造成严重污染——都会提高感染风险。

points.en: Field practice: never assume a bullet travelled a straight path — it can ricochet inside the body, especially off bone; scene safety and patient care always outrank gathering forensic details like weapon type, range, or ammunition, though passing that information to the trauma team when safely available is still useful.
points.zh: 现场操作：绝不要假设子弹走了直线——它可能在体内反弹，尤其是撞到骨头之后；现场安全和病人照护永远比收集武器型号、射击距离、弹药种类等法证细节更优先，但在安全的前提下，把这些信息带给创伤团队仍然有价值。

points.en: Five blast-injury mechanisms: primary (damage from the pressure wave itself), secondary (struck by flying debris/shrapnel, which can travel up to nearly 5,000 km/h for conventional military explosives), tertiary (the patient's body is hurled by blast wind against a stationary object, which can amputate limbs), quaternary (burns, toxic-gas inhalation, crush injury from structural collapse, and prolonged entrapment), and quinary (biologic, chemical, or radioactive contaminants added to the device, as in a 'dirty bomb').
points.zh: 五种爆炸伤机制：原发性（冲击波本身造成的损伤）、继发性（被飞散的碎片/弹片击中，常规军用炸药的碎片可飞至近 5,000 km/h）、三发性（爆炸风把病人身体甩向静止物体，可致断肢）、四发性（烧伤、有毒气体吸入伤、建筑倒塌造成的挤压伤、长时间被困）、五发性（装置中添加的生物、化学或放射性污染物，即「脏弹」）。

points.en: Physics: detonation converts a solid or liquid into large volumes of pressurized gas; Composition C4 can generate initial pressures over 27.5 million kilopascals, producing a spherical blast wave. The positive wave pulse (pressure above atmospheric) is the main injurious phase; the negative wave pulse (below atmospheric) can last about 10 times longer and drives high-velocity return winds.
points.zh: 物理原理：爆炸把固体或液体转化为大量高压气体；C4 炸药初始压力可超过 2,750 万千帕，形成球形冲击波。正压相（高于大气压）是主要致伤阶段；负压相（低于大气压）可持续约正压相的 10 倍时长，并驱动高速回流风。

points.en: Wave speed/duration/pressure depend on charge size (bigger = faster, longer wave), the surrounding medium (faster in water than air), distance from the blast (farther = slower, longer duration), and reflecting surfaces (a pressure wave reflected off a wall can multiply several times — standing beside a wall is more dangerous than standing in the open).
points.zh: 冲击波的速度/持续时间/压力取决于炸药量大小（越大＝波越快越持久）、周围介质（水中比空气中传播更快）、距爆炸点的距离（越远＝波越慢、持续越久），以及反射面（压力波撞到墙壁等反射面可能被放大数倍——站在墙边比站在空旷处更危险）。

points.en: Blast-wind missile thresholds: about 15 m/sec can penetrate human skin, and about 120 m/sec can enter a major body cavity and cause serious internal injury; blast winds themselves can exceed 100 m/sec.
points.zh: 爆炸风携带的抛射物阈值：约 15 m/sec 就能穿透人体皮肤，约 120 m/sec 就能进入体腔造成严重内伤；爆炸风本身速度可超过 100 m/sec。

points.en: Underwater explosions injure at about 3 times the distance of an open-air blast of the same size (higher positive pressure, no negative-pressure/wind phase), though fragments and gases travel shorter distances in water. Explosions in closed spaces are worse overall because forces cannot dissipate and toxic gas/smoke accumulates; a wave hitting a solid surface can fragment the denser medium (spalling) or compress and re-expand trapped gas bubbles (implosion), each adding injury.
points.zh: 水下爆炸的致伤距离约是同等规模空气中爆炸的 3 倍（正压更高，没有负压/风相），但碎片和气体在水中传播的距离反而更短。密闭空间内的爆炸整体更危险，因为力量无法消散，还会积聚有毒气体和烟雾；冲击波撞到坚实表面时，可能使较致密的介质碎裂（层裂）或压缩再膨胀被困气泡（内爆），两者都会加重损伤。

points.en: The ear is the organ most sensitive to blast: the tympanic membrane ruptures at just 0.35 kg/cm2 above atmospheric pressure, so ear pain, ringing, hearing loss, or blood in the canal is a sensitive marker for other, less visible blast injury — including the lungs.
points.zh: 耳朵是对爆炸最敏感的器官：鼓膜在高出大气压仅 0.35 kg/cm2 时就会破裂，所以耳痛、耳鸣、听力下降或耳道出血，是提示其他不明显爆炸伤（包括肺部）的敏感信号。

points.en: Primary pulmonary blast injury (contusion/hemorrhage) may be unilateral in open spaces but bilateral in confined spaces; watch for chest tightness or pain, hemoptysis, tachypnea, and subcutaneous emphysema. Pneumothorax may need field decompression; positive-pressure ventilation can be rapidly fatal unless the pneumothorax is drained, and IV fluids are poorly tolerated and can precipitate pulmonary edema.
points.zh: 原发性肺爆震伤（挫伤/出血）在开放空间可能是单侧，在密闭空间常是双侧；要警惕胸闷或胸痛、咯血、呼吸急促和皮下气肿。气胸可能需要现场减压；除非气胸已引流，正压通气可能迅速致命，静脉补液耐受性差，可能诱发肺水肿。

points.en: Arterial air embolism from alveolar disruption is one of the most dangerous pulmonary blast complications: air entering a coronary artery causes myocardial injury, while air entering the cerebrovascular system produces vision changes, behaviour changes, altered consciousness, and other neurologic signs.
points.zh: 肺泡破裂造成的动脉空气栓塞是最危险的肺爆震并发症之一：空气进入冠状动脉会造成心肌损伤，进入脑血管系统则会出现视力改变、行为改变、意识改变等各种神经系统表现。

points.en: Solid abdominal organs are relatively protected from the shock wave itself (but vulnerable to secondary missiles); hollow organs like bowel can perforate or rupture similarly to lung tissue, and underwater blasts cause the most severe abdominal injuries. Neurologic injury (subarachnoid/subdural hematoma) is a leading cause of blast death; transient loss of consciousness can come from head trauma or from a vagally mediated cardiogenic-shock-like picture (bradycardia plus hypotension without compensatory vasoconstriction) that commonly follows an intense pressure wave.
points.zh: 实质性腹腔器官相对不受冲击波本身影响（但容易被继发弹片击中）；空腔器官如肠道可能像肺组织一样穿孔或破裂，水下爆炸造成的腹部损伤最严重。神经系统损伤（蛛网膜下腔/硬膜下血肿）是爆炸致死的主要原因之一；一过性意识丧失可能来自头外伤，也可能来自强烈冲击波后常见的迷走神经介导的心源性休克样表现（心动过缓加低血压、没有代偿性血管收缩）。

points.en: Extremity injury including traumatic amputation is common (tertiary mechanism); body armour reduces torso shrapnel death but 'catches' more blast-wave energy, which can throw the wearer backward and raise the risk of spine and spinal-cord injury, alongside more severe orthopedic/extremity injuries among survivors.
points.zh: 肢体损伤包括创伤性截肢很常见（三发性机制）；防弹衣能减少躯干弹片致死，但会「吸收」更多冲击波能量，可能把穿戴者向后掀倒，提高脊柱和脊髓损伤的风险，幸存者也因此更常见严重的骨科/肢体损伤。

points.en: The platinum 10 minutes is the goal for maximum scene time with a critical trauma patient (barring extended extrication); evidence shows on-scene stabilization is rarely indicated and is usually associated with a worse outcome — 'scoop and run' remains the best approach.
points.zh: 「铂金 10 分钟」是危重创伤病人现场停留时间的目标上限（除非需要长时间解救）；有证据显示现场「稳定处理」很少有指征，通常反而带来更差的结局——「铲起就走」仍然是最佳做法。

points.en: Accreditation Canada's Trauma Distinction program has five levels (I-V); Levels I-III are recognized trauma centres (I-II for pediatric trauma). Level I provides the highest level of care including complex subspecialty (quaternary) trauma care, leadership, research, teaching, data/registry participation, and injury-prevention programs. Level II is an urban/community hospital treating single-system and some multisystem injury, referring complex cases to Level I. Level III is a smaller hospital serving as an initial stabilization/triage facility, referring all but isolated minor injuries onward. Level IV is bypassed in urban settings in favour of a nearby trauma centre; Level V is a rural hospital that promptly transfers patients to a trauma centre.
points.zh: 加拿大医疗机构认证局（Accreditation Canada）的创伤认证计划分五级（I-V）；I-III 级被认定为创伤中心（儿科创伤为 I-II 级）。I 级提供最高级别照护，包括复杂亚专科（四级）创伤救治、领导角色、科研、教学、数据/登记参与和伤害预防项目。II 级是城市/社区医院，能治单系统和部分多系统损伤，复杂病例转诊至 I 级。III 级是较小医院，作为初步稳定/分诊机构，除孤立轻伤外都转诊出去。IV 级在城市环境中会被绕过、改送附近的创伤中心；V 级是乡村医院，会迅速把病人转往创伤中心。

points.en: The (Canadian-adapted) CDC field-triage decision tree has four steps. Step 1 physiologic (route to the highest-level trauma centre): GCS 13 or less, SBP under 90 mm Hg, respiratory rate under 10 or over 29 per minute (under 20/min in an infant under 1 year), or need for ventilatory support.
points.zh: （加拿大版）CDC 现场分诊决策树共四步。第一步生理标准（送往最高级创伤中心）：GCS ≤13、收缩压 <90 mm Hg、呼吸频率 <10 或 >29 次/分（1 岁以下婴儿 <20 次/分），或需要通气支持。

points.en: Step 2 anatomic (route to the highest-level trauma centre): any penetrating injury to head/neck/torso/extremities proximal to the elbow or knee; chest-wall instability or deformity (flail chest); two or more proximal long-bone fractures; a crushed, degloved, mangled, or pulseless extremity; amputation proximal to the wrist or ankle; pelvic fracture; open or depressed skull fracture; or paralysis.
points.zh: 第二步解剖学标准（送往最高级创伤中心）：头/颈/躯干/肘或膝以上肢体的任何穿透伤；胸壁不稳定或畸形（连枷胸）；两处或以上近端长骨骨折；肢体挤压、撕脱、毁损或无脉搏；腕或踝以上的截肢；骨盆骨折；开放性或凹陷性颅骨骨折；或瘫痪。

points.en: Step 3 mechanism (route to A designated trauma centre, not necessarily Level I, per the textbook's Canadian adaptation): adult fall over 6 m (child over 3 m or 2-3 times the child's height); high-risk auto collision (intrusion over 30 cm on the occupant site or over 45 cm at any site, ejection, death in the same passenger compartment, or high-risk telemetry data); vehicle-versus-pedestrian/cyclist thrown, run over, or hit at over 35 km/h; motorcycle crash over 35 km/h. Step 4 special considerations (judgment-based): age over 55, SBP under 110 possibly signalling shock after 65, low-impact mechanisms in the elderly, pediatric-capable centres for children, anticoagulant use with head injury, burns (isolated to burn centre, combined with trauma to trauma centre), pregnancy over 20 weeks, and EMS provider judgment.
points.zh: 第三步机制标准（教材的加拿大版：送往一家指定创伤中心，不一定是 I 级）：成人坠落 >6 m（儿童 >3 m 或超过身高 2-3 倍）；高危车祸（乘员侧侵入 >30 cm 或任意部位侵入 >45 cm、被抛出、同车厢内有人死亡，或车载遥测数据显示高风险）；机动车撞行人/骑车人并将其抛出、碾压，或撞击速度 >35 km/h；摩托车事故 >35 km/h。第四步特殊考量（凭判断）：55 岁以上、65 岁以上收缩压 <110 可能已是休克、老年人低能量机制也可能造成重伤、儿童送有儿科能力的中心、抗凝药合并头外伤、烧伤（单纯烧伤送烧伤中心，合并创伤送创伤中心）、孕 20 周以上，以及急救人员的现场判断。

points.en: Transport principle: send the patient to the nearest MOST APPROPRIATE facility, not simply the nearest facility — sometimes that means bypassing a closer non-trauma hospital for a farther Level I/II centre when the patient's needs demand it. The Canadian National Trauma Registry (Trauma Association of Canada plus the Canadian Institute for Health Information) collects trauma data for quality, cost-effectiveness, and outcomes research — your scene documentation feeds directly into it.
points.zh: 转运原则：送往最近的「最合适」机构，而不是单纯最近的机构——有时这意味着绕过较近的非创伤医院，送往较远的 I/II 级创伤中心，前提是病人的需求要求这样做。加拿大国家创伤登记系统（创伤协会加加拿大健康信息研究所）收集创伤数据用于质量改进、成本效益分析和结局研究——你在现场写的记录会直接进入这个系统。

points.en: Air medical transport should be considered for: extended ground transport time; distance/geography that makes ground transport infeasible; prolonged extrication of a critically injured patient; or the need for a critical procedure or higher scope of practice en route — weigh launch-plus-flight-plus-landing time against ground time, and check for a safe landing zone, before calling.
points.zh: 考虑空中转运的情况：陆路转运耗时过长；距离/地形使陆路转运不可行；重伤病人的救援/解救耗时过长；或途中需要关键处置或更高执业范围的操作——呼叫前要把「起飞＋飞行＋降落」的总时间和陆路时间做比较，并确认有安全的降落区。

points.en: Relative contraindications for air medical transport: patients unlikely to survive (e.g. traumatic cardiac arrest), combative patients who are not intubated/paralysed, morbidly obese patients, barotrauma/diving injuries (which need a lower flying altitude), bad weather, or situations where ground transport reaches an equal or better level of care faster.
points.zh: 空中转运的相对禁忌：不太可能存活的病人（如创伤性心脏骤停）、未插管/未使用肌松剂的躁动病人、病态肥胖病人、气压伤/潜水伤（需要更低飞行高度）、恶劣天气，或陆路转运能更快达到同等或更好照护水平的情况。

sections.titleEn: Updates in Resuscitation: Permissive Hypotension, Prehospital Blood, and TXA
sections.titleZh: 复苏新进展：允许性低血压、院前血制品与 TXA

points.en: Rationale for permissive hypotension: aggressive early crystalloid in hemorrhagic shock can raise BP enough to dislodge fresh clots and worsen bleeding, while also diluting circulating blood and clotting factors (dilutional coagulopathy). A landmark study roughly 25 years ago challenged routine early prehospital/ED crystalloid administration in favour of delayed resuscitation just before definitive hemorrhage control — do not delay transport to start an IV purely for fluid resuscitation.
points.zh: 允许性低血压的依据：出血性休克早期大量输注晶体液，可能把血压推高到冲开新形成的血凝块、加重出血，同时还会稀释循环中的血液和凝血因子（稀释性凝血障碍）。约 25 年前的一项里程碑研究，质疑了常规院前/急诊早期晶体液输注的做法，转而支持延迟到确定性止血前才补液——不要为了单纯补液而耽误转运去开静脉。

points.en: The strategy balances tissue hypoperfusion against dilutional coagulopathy and rebleeding before definitive hemorrhage control; the textbook frames the likely benefit as greatest for penetrating torso/extremity trauma and potentially harmful for severe brain injury, where perfusion pressure must be protected. Textbook-cited pressure thresholds: crystalloid may be started once SBP falls under 70 mm Hg for most trauma patients, or under 90 mm Hg if a serious head injury is suspected — the actual BC-tested numbers differ (see BC alerts and Chapter 21).
points.zh: 这个策略是在「确定性止血前的组织低灌注」与「稀释性凝血障碍和再出血」之间找平衡；教材认为穿透性躯干/肢体创伤获益可能最大，而严重脑外伤可能因需要保住灌注压而受害。教材给出的血压阈值：多数创伤病人收缩压 <70 mm Hg 才开始补晶体液，怀疑严重头外伤则是 <90 mm Hg——BC 实际考的数字并不一样（见 BC 差异栏和第 21 章）。

points.en: Prehospital blood products: evidence is not yet conclusive, and a rapid, limited scene assessment makes it hard to reliably identify which patients have massive ongoing hemorrhage severe enough to benefit. In practice, field blood-product administration is currently mostly limited to air medical and land critical-care services, or research protocols — follow your local and regional protocol.
points.zh: 院前血制品：证据还不够充分，而且现场评估快速又有限，很难可靠识别出真正需要血制品的大量持续出血病人。目前院前血制品给药大多局限在空中医疗和陆地重症转运团队，或研究性方案——以当地和区域协议为准。

points.en: TXA history and evidence: this synthetic clot-stabilizing agent was discovered in the 1950s; combat-setting studies show a survival benefit, but routine EMS use is not yet confirmed. It likely benefits a subgroup of patients with severe uncontrolled hemorrhage, but that subgroup is difficult to identify prospectively — follow local and regional protocol (BC's full monograph, including the 2 g IV push over 1 minute and its contraindications, is covered in Chapter 21).
points.zh: TXA 的历史与证据：这种合成止血稳定剂在 1950 年代被发现；战地研究显示能提高生存率，但常规 EMS 使用尚未得到确认。它可能对一部分有严重难控出血的病人有益，但很难前瞻性地识别出这个亚组——以当地和区域协议为准（BC 的完整用药单，包括 2 g 静推、用时 1 分钟及其禁忌证，见第 21 章）。

points.en: The trauma lethal triad — hypothermia, coagulopathy (poor clotting), and acidosis — is a major contributor to death from severe traumatic bleeding; even mildly hypothermic patients have a lower survival rate than normothermic ones.
points.zh: 创伤死亡三联征——低体温、凝血障碍（凝血功能差）、酸中毒——是严重创伤性出血致死的重要原因；即使只是轻度低体温，患者存活率也会低于体温正常的患者。

points.en: The self-reinforcing cycle: hypothermia worsens coagulopathy, poor clotting allows more blood loss than would otherwise occur, that blood loss deepens acidosis (pH under 7.35) — and acidosis in turn further impairs clotting. Treatments themselves can feed the cycle: normal saline, commonly bolused for hypotension, is itself quite acidic.
points.zh: 自我加重的循环：低体温使凝血障碍恶化，凝血差导致失血超出正常应有的量，失血又加深酸中毒（pH <7.35）——而酸中毒反过来进一步削弱凝血功能。治疗本身也可能加重这个循环：常用来纠正低血压的生理盐水，本身就偏酸性。

points.en: Field countermeasures: aggressively control all bleeding (don't hesitate to apply a tourniquet to a limb if initial attempts fail); keep the patient warm with blankets both under and over them, and warm IV fluids to at least normal body temperature; minimize the volume of acidic IV fluid given; monitor end-tidal CO2 and ventilation to avoid respiratory acidosis; and consider TXA per protocol to help control internal bleeding.
points.zh: 现场对策：积极控制所有出血（初步止血无效时不要犹豫上止血带）；用毯子上下都盖来保暖，静脉输液加温到至少正常体温；尽量减少所输酸性液体的量；监测呼气末二氧化碳和通气以避免呼吸性酸中毒；并按协议考虑使用 TXA 帮助控制内出血。

atScene.en: A cracked windshield, damaged steering wheel/dashboard, vehicle intrusion, or fractured feet/ankles after a fall should all raise suspicion for spinal injury and change how you manage the primary survey.
atScene.zh: 挡风玻璃裂、方向盘或仪表板损坏、车厢侵入，或坠落后出现足/踝骨折——都应提高对脊柱损伤的怀疑，并改变你处理初评的方式。

atScene.en: Notes from Nancy, twice: damage to the steering assembly means critical injury to the driver until proven otherwise; a cracked or broken windshield means the front-seat occupant has a cervical-spine injury until proven otherwise.
atScene.zh: Nancy 的两句提醒：方向盘组件受损＝司机有严重损伤，除非证明不是；挡风玻璃裂了或碎了＝前排乘员有颈椎损伤，除非证明不是。

atScene.en: Never label a wound 'entry' or 'exit' in your documentation — describe only the location, size, and shape of what you see; your record can end up in a courtroom.
atScene.zh: 记录中绝不要把伤口标成「入口」或「出口」——只描述你看到的位置、大小和形状；你的记录可能会被搬上法庭。

atScene.en: Never assume a bullet travelled a straight path between entry and exit — it can ricochet inside the body, especially off bone, and travel in unpredictable directions.
atScene.zh: 绝不要假设子弹在入口和出口之间走了直线——它可能在体内反弹（尤其撞到骨头后），朝不可预测的方向走。

atScene.en: Ear symptoms (ringing, pain, hearing loss, blood in the canal) after an explosion should make you look hard for lung injury on the same patient — the two travel together.
atScene.zh: 爆炸后出现耳部症状（耳鸣、耳痛、听力下降、耳道出血），要立刻高度怀疑同一病人存在肺损伤——这两者常常一起出现。

atScene.en: A dislocated knee after a pedestrian strike should be splinted in the position found if distal PMS is intact — but if it spontaneously reduces, you must report that verbally AND in writing; spontaneous reduction is a red flag for vascular injury the trauma team could otherwise miss.
atScene.zh: 行人被撞后的膝关节脱位，如果远端 PMS 完好，应按发现时的姿势固定——但如果它自行复位了，必须口头加书面双重报告；自行复位是血管损伤的红旗信号，不报告团队可能会漏诊。

atScene.en: The platinum 10 minutes: minimize scene time for a critical trauma patient unless extrication genuinely demands more. On-scene 'stabilization' is rarely indicated and is usually associated with a worse outcome — scoop and run.
atScene.zh: 铂金 10 分钟：除非解救确实需要更久，否则要把危重创伤病人的现场时间压到最短。现场「稳定处理」很少有指征，通常反而带来更差的结局——铲起就走。

atScene.en: Before calling for air medical transport, weigh the launch-plus-flight-plus-landing time against ground transport time, and confirm there is a safe landing zone — if ground transport reaches definitive care in reasonable time with no critical en-route procedure needed, air transport is not required.
atScene.zh: 呼叫空中转运前，先把「起飞＋飞行＋降落」的总时间和陆路转运时间做比较，并确认有安全的降落区——如果陆路能在合理时间内到达确定性治疗、途中也不需要关键处置，就不需要叫空中转运。

confusions.en: 'No visible external damage means no serious injury' — wrong: blunt force spread over a wide contact area can rupture the spleen or tear the aorta while leaving almost no external mark.
confusions.zh: 「体表没明显损伤＝没有严重损伤」——错：钝性力量分散在大面积接触上，可能已经把脾脏撞裂或把主动脉撕开，体表却几乎看不出来。

confusions.en: Labelling wounds as 'entry' or 'exit' is not your job in the field — multiple wounds may come from one projectile that passed through, or from two separate ones; guessing and documenting a label can mislead the criminal investigation.
confusions.zh: 在现场给伤口贴「入口/出口」标签不是你的工作——多个伤口可能来自一枚穿透弹丸，也可能来自两次独立的伤害；猜错并写进记录可能会误导刑事调查。

confusions.en: 'A motorcycle helmet protects the neck' — false: it protects the skull from direct impact but transmits that force straight into the cervical spine; it does NOT protect against severe cervical injury.
confusions.zh: 「摩托车头盔能保护颈部」——错：它能防止头骨受到直接撞击，但会把这股力量直接传入颈椎；它并不能防止严重的颈椎损伤。

confusions.en: 'Seat belts increase fetal injury risk in pregnancy' is a myth — proper lap-plus-shoulder belt use decreases both maternal and fetal injury; the real danger is a lap belt worn alone and too high, across the belly instead of low across the pelvis.
confusions.zh: 「孕妇系安全带会增加胎儿损伤风险」是迷思——正确使用腰带＋肩带能同时降低母体和胎儿损伤；真正的危险是只系腰带、而且系得太高，压在肚子上而不是压低在骨盆上。

confusions.en: The Trauma Score is not the universal go-to tool — it fails to predict survival in severe isolated head injury because motor and verbal deficits confound its GCS component; the Revised Trauma Score (RTS) is built for exactly that situation.
confusions.zh: 创伤评分（Trauma Score）不是万能工具——它在严重孤立性头外伤时预测不准，因为运动和语言反应会被头伤本身干扰其中的 GCS 部分；改良创伤评分（RTS）就是为这种情况设计的。

confusions.en: A rollover with seat belts worn is not automatically 'safe' — injuries can still be serious with every direction change; belts mainly cut the risk of ejection, not the risk of injury from repeated impacts inside the cabin.
confusions.zh: 翻滚车祸系了安全带不代表「安全」——每变一次方向乘员都会再被撞一次，伤情仍可能很重；安全带主要降低的是被甩出车外的风险，不是车内反复撞击造成的损伤风险。

confusions.en: 'Water is soft, so a high fall onto water is safer than onto concrete' — false at high speed: water has almost no plasticity on high-velocity impact and behaves close to a rigid surface.
confusions.zh: 「水很软，高处落水比落在混凝土上安全」——高速撞击下是错的：水在高速冲击下几乎没有可塑性，表现得接近坚硬表面。

confusions.en: The book's CDC field-triage numbers (GCS<=13, intrusion 45 cm, pedestrian/cyclist/motorcycle 35 km/h) are the TEXTBOOK's Canadian-adapted criteria for trauma-centre destination — BC's practical-exam 'automatically unstable' mechanism list uses different cut numbers (see BC Alerts). Do not mix the two frameworks in one answer.
confusions.zh: 教材的 CDC 现场分诊数字（GCS≤13、侵入 45 cm、行人/骑车人/摩托车 35 km/h）是教材版的加拿大改编标准，用来决定送哪一级创伤中心——BC 实操考的「自动判不稳定」机制清单用的是不同的切点数字（见 BC 差异栏）。答题时不要把两套框架混着用。

confusions.en: 'Permissive hypotension applies to every trauma patient' — false: it is contraindicated (or at least unproven) in traumatic brain injury, children, pregnancy, and the elderly; the full BC protocol numbers live in Chapter 21, not this chapter.
confusions.zh: 「允许性低血压适用于所有创伤病人」——错：它在创伤性脑损伤、儿童、孕妇和老年人中是禁忌（或至少缺乏证据支持）；BC 完整的协议数字在第 21 章，不在本章。

mnemonics.name: V-O-O-S-A
mnemonics.en: Five phases of MVC trauma in order: Vehicle deceleration, Occupant deceleration, Organ deceleration, Secondary impacts, Additional impacts.
mnemonics.zh: 机动车碰撞创伤五阶段顺序：车（辆减速）、乘（员减速）、脏（器减速）、二（次撞击）、再（次撞击）。

mnemonics.name: F-L-R-R-R
mnemonics.en: Five impact patterns: Frontal, Lateral, Rear, Rotational, Rollover.
mnemonics.zh: 五种撞击模式：正面、侧面、追尾、旋转、翻滚——按字母 F-L-R-R-R 记。

mnemonics.name: 1-2-3-4-5 blast
mnemonics.en: Blast mechanisms count how far removed from the raw pressure wave they are: 1 primary (the wave itself), 2 secondary (debris it throws), 3 tertiary (the patient it throws), 4 quaternary (burns/crush/toxic fallout), 5 quinary (contaminants riding along).
mnemonics.zh: 爆炸伤机制的数字，代表离原始冲击波有多「远」：1 原发（冲击波本身）、2 继发（它抛出的碎片）、3 三发（它抛出的病人）、4 四发（烧伤/挤压/毒气等次生后果）、5 五发（搭便车的污染物）。

mnemonics.name: Waddell = 盆-胸-头
mnemonics.en: Waddell triad in child pedestrians strikes bottom-up: pelvis/femur first (bumper), chest/abdomen second (hood/grille), head last (vehicle then ground) — the opposite order from an adult's knee-hood-ground sequence.
mnemonics.zh: Waddell 三联征在儿童行人身上是自下而上：先盆/股（保险杠），再胸/腹（引擎盖/格栅），最后头（先撞车再撞地）——和成人「膝-引擎盖-地面」的顺序正好相反。

mnemonics.name: 冷-稀-酸
mnemonics.en: Trauma lethal triad: hypothermia (cold), coagulopathy (thin/poor clotting), acidosis (sour) — each one feeds the other two.
mnemonics.zh: 创伤死亡三联征：低体温（冷）、凝血障碍（稀/凝不住）、酸中毒（酸）——三者互相喂养。

mnemonics.name: KE = 1/2 mv^2
mnemonics.en: Velocity is squared, mass is not — doubling speed is far deadlier than doubling weight.
mnemonics.zh: 速度是平方项，质量不是——车速翻倍比体重翻倍致命得多。

selfCheck.qEn: Compare the kinetic energy of a 70-kg person struck at 55 km/h vs 65 km/h. What does the size of that jump teach you about judging MOI severity?
selfCheck.qZh: 对比 70 kg 的人以 55 km/h 和 65 km/h 被撞时的动能。这个跳跃的幅度，对你判断受伤机制严重度有什么启示？
selfCheck.aEn: About 211,750 KE units at 55 km/h versus about 295,750 at 65 km/h — an increase of roughly 84,000 units from just 10 km/h more speed, far larger than the change from adding 10 kg of body weight at a constant speed. Velocity dominates injury severity assessment because kinetic energy scales with velocity squared, not mass.
selfCheck.aZh: 55 km/h 时约 211,750 动能单位，65 km/h 时约 295,750——仅仅多 10 km/h 就多出约 84,000 单位，远大于同速度下多 10 kg 体重带来的变化。速度对损伤严重度判断的影响远大于质量，因为动能与速度的平方成正比，与质量只是一次方关系。

selfCheck.qEn: State BC's three mechanism-of-injury cut-offs for an automatically-unstable trauma patient, and name where they diverge from the textbook's CDC-adapted field-triage numbers.
selfCheck.qZh: 背出 BC 判定「自动不稳定」创伤病人的三条受伤机制切点，并说出它们和教材 CDC 现场分诊数字的两处分歧。
selfCheck.aEn: BC: free fall over 6 m; vehicle intrusion over 0.3 m on the occupant site or over 0.5 m at any site including the roof (or ejection, or death in the passenger compartment); auto-versus-pedestrian/cyclist or motorcycle crash over 30 kph. Divergence from the book: any-site intrusion is 45 cm in the book versus 50 cm in BC, and pedestrian/cyclist/motorcycle speed is 35 km/h in the book versus 30 kph in BC — answer with BC's numbers on the exam.
selfCheck.aZh: BC：自由坠落 >6 m；车厢侵入乘员侧 >0.3 m 或任意部位（含车顶）>0.5 m（或被抛出、或同车厢有人死亡）；机动车撞行人/骑车人或摩托车事故 >30 kph。和教材的分歧：任意部位侵入教材是 45 cm、BC 是 50 cm；行人/骑车人/摩托车速度教材是 35 km/h、BC 是 30 kph——考试按 BC 数字答。

selfCheck.qEn: Using the book's 3.5-m-per-storey assumption, roughly what fall heights correspond to 50% and 90% mortality?
selfCheck.qZh: 按教材「每层楼 3.5 m」的假设，大约多高的坠落分别对应 50% 和 90% 的死亡率？
selfCheck.aEn: About 4 storeys (roughly 14 m) kills roughly 50% of fallers; about 7 storeys (roughly 24.5 m) kills roughly 90%.
selfCheck.aZh: 约 4 层楼高（约 14 m）会导致约 50% 的坠落者死亡；约 7 层楼高（约 24.5 m）会导致约 90% 死亡。

selfCheck.qEn: Explain the paper-bag syndrome mechanism in a frontal MVC, and state roughly what share of steering-wheel-related pneumothoraces it accounts for.
selfCheck.qZh: 解释正面车祸中「纸袋综合征」的机制，并说出它大约占方向盘相关气胸的多大比例。
selfCheck.aEn: The occupant reflexively takes a deep breath just before impact, closing the glottis and hyperinflating the lungs; the steering wheel then strikes the chest, and the trapped pressure ruptures alveoli, producing a pneumothorax. This mechanism is estimated to account for 60% to 70% of steering-wheel-related pneumothoraces.
selfCheck.aZh: 乘员在撞击前反射性深吸气，声门关闭、肺过度充气；方向盘随后撞击胸部，被困住的压力把肺泡撑破，形成气胸。这个机制估计占方向盘相关气胸的 60%-70%。

selfCheck.qEn: Name the trauma lethal triad and explain how its three components reinforce each other.
selfCheck.qZh: 说出创伤死亡三联征的三个组成部分，并解释它们之间如何互相加重。
selfCheck.aEn: Hypothermia, coagulopathy, and acidosis (pH under 7.35). Cold blood clots poorly (coagulopathy), poor clotting allows more blood loss than would otherwise occur, extra blood loss deepens acidosis, and acidosis further impairs clotting — each element worsens the other two, and treatment itself (acidic normal saline) can feed the cycle unless bleeding control, active warming, and minimal acidic fluid are all used together.
selfCheck.aZh: 低体温、凝血障碍、酸中毒（pH <7.35）。血冷了凝不住（凝血障碍），凝血差就会比原本失血更多，多失的血又加深酸中毒，酸中毒再反过来削弱凝血——三者互相加重，而治疗本身（偏酸的生理盐水）如果不搭配止血、主动保暖、少给酸性液体，还会反过来喂养这个循环。

bcAlerts.topicZh: 「自动判不稳定」的受伤机制数字
bcAlerts.bookEn: The CDC-adapted Step 3 field-triage criteria (Canadian version): adult fall over 6 m (child over 3 m or 2-3x height); vehicle intrusion over 30 cm on the occupant site or over 45 cm at any site including the roof; ejection; death in the passenger compartment; auto-versus-pedestrian/cyclist thrown, run over, or impacted at over 35 km/h; motorcycle crash over 35 km/h. These route the patient to A designated trauma centre, not necessarily Level I.
bcAlerts.bookZh: 教材的 CDC 改编版第三步「机制」分诊标准（加拿大版）：成人坠落 >6 m（儿童 >3 m 或超过身高 2-3 倍）；车厢侵入乘员侧 >30 cm 或任意部位（含车顶）>45 cm；被抛出；同车厢内有人死亡；机动车撞行人/骑车人并将其抛出、碾压或撞击速度 >35 km/h；摩托车事故 >35 km/h。这些标准会把病人送到「一家指定创伤中心」，不一定是 I 级。
bcAlerts.bcEn: BC's practical-exam 'unstable adult patient — mechanism of injury' list uses different cut numbers: free fall over 6 m (same as the book); intrusion over 0.3 m on the occupant side (matches the book's 30 cm) but over 0.5 m at any site including the roof (NOT 45 cm); auto-versus-pedestrian/cyclist over 30 kph (NOT 35 km/h); motorcycle crash over 30 kph (NOT 35 km/h). Any one of these alone makes the patient unstable — load and go, treat en route.
bcAlerts.bcZh: BC 实操考「不稳定成人病人——受伤机制」清单用的是不同的切点：自由坠落 >6 m（和教材一致）；车厢侵入乘员侧 >0.3 m（和教材的 30 cm 一致），但任意部位（含车顶）是 >0.5 m（不是 45 cm）；机动车撞行人/骑车人 >30 kph（不是 35 km/h）；摩托车事故 >30 kph（不是 35 km/h）。满足任意一条即判不稳定——立即装载转运，处置放在车上做。
bcAlerts.ref: BC Guidelines p.7-8 Findings in Unstable Adult Patients — Mechanism of Injury

bcAlerts.bookEn: The textbook uses a 4-step CDC field-triage algorithm (Physiologic / Anatomic / Mechanism / Special considerations) to decide trauma-centre destination, with numeric GCS, SBP, and respiratory-rate cut-offs at Step 1.
bcAlerts.bookZh: 教材用的是四步 CDC 现场分诊算法（生理／解剖／机制／特殊考量），第一步用 GCS、收缩压和呼吸频率的数字切点来判断。
bcAlerts.bcEn: BC's practical exam does NOT test the CDC 4-step algorithm — it uses its own three-category list at p.7-8 (Primary Survey findings / Anatomical findings / Mechanism of injury). The primary-survey category is descriptive, not numeric: altered LOC or unconsciousness, difficulty maintaining the airway, respiratory distress, absent radial pulses, cardiac arrest, hemorrhage needing a tourniquet or wound packing, cool pale clammy skin from suspected shock, suspected CVA, heat stroke, severe hypothermia, suspected cardiac chest pain, and anaphylaxis. Study BC's list for the practical station, not the book's numeric algorithm.
bcAlerts.bcZh: BC 实操考不考 CDC 四步算法——它用自己在 p.7-8 的三分类清单（初检发现／解剖学发现／受伤机制）。初检发现这一类是描述性的，不是数字化的：意识改变或无反应、维持气道困难、呼吸窘迫、桡动脉消失、心脏骤停、需要止血带或伤口填塞的出血、疑休克的湿冷苍白皮肤、疑似 CVA、中暑、重度低体温、疑似心源性胸痛、过敏反应。实操站要背 BC 的清单，不是教材的数字算法。
bcAlerts.ref: BC Guidelines p.7 Findings in Unstable Adult Patients

bcAlerts.topicZh: 允许性低血压的血压目标
bcAlerts.bookEn: This chapter frames crystalloid infusion as starting once SBP falls under 70 mm Hg for most trauma patients, or under 90 mm Hg if a serious head injury is suspected; ITLS is cited as recommending avoidance of hypotension in TBI and delaying aggressive fluids to hospital arrival for suspected active hemorrhage.
bcAlerts.bookZh: 本章的说法是：多数创伤病人收缩压 <70 mm Hg 才开始输晶体液，怀疑严重头外伤则是 <90 mm Hg；并引用 ITLS 的建议——TBI 要避免低血压，疑似活动性出血则把积极补液延后到医院。
bcAlerts.bcEn: BC's actual protocol numbers differ and are the ones to answer with: target SBP around 70-80 (or titrate to 80-90) with fresh-clot preservation in mind, contraindicated in TBI where BC instead demands SBP above 120 (the book only demands above 90). Full detail lives in Chapter 21's bcAlerts — this chapter only needs to flag that the book's threshold numbers are not the tested ones.
bcAlerts.bcZh: BC 的实际协议数字不一样，考试要用这套：目标收缩压约 70-80（或滴定至 80-90），为了保住新形成的血凝块；TBI 是禁忌，BC 要求收缩压保在 120 以上（教材只要求 90 以上）。完整细节在第 21 章的 BC 差异栏——本章只需要记住教材的阈值数字不是考试答案。
bcAlerts.ref: cross-reference: see Chapter 21 bcAlerts; BC Guidelines p.27 Traumatic Brain Injuries

bcAlerts.topicEn: TXA: 'per protocol' versus a full monograph
bcAlerts.topicZh: TXA：教材只说「按协议」，BC 有完整用药单
bcAlerts.bookEn: This chapter introduces TXA only as an emerging-evidence topic: 'refer to local and regional protocols regarding TXA use' — no dose, route, or contraindications given.
bcAlerts.bookZh: 本章只把 TXA 当作一个新兴证据话题介绍：「TXA 的使用请参照当地和区域协议」——没有给出剂量、途径或禁忌证。
bcAlerts.bcEn: BC has a full testable monograph, not just a protocol pointer: 2 g IV push over 1 minute; contraindicated if allergy, more than 3 hours since injury, under 12 years old, or isolated TBI. This is directly examinable — full detail is in Chapter 21's bcAlerts, but do not walk into the exam thinking TXA is a 'check local protocol, no fixed answer' topic.
bcAlerts.bcZh: BC 有一份完整的、可考的用药单，不只是「查协议」这么简单：2 g 静脉推注、用时 1 分钟；过敏、伤后超过 3 小时、12 岁以下、孤立性 TBI 均为禁忌。这是直接会考的内容——完整细节在第 21 章的 BC 差异栏，但不要以为 TXA 是「查当地协议、没有固定答案」的话题。
bcAlerts.ref: cross-reference: see Chapter 21 bcAlerts; BC Guidelines p.78 Tranexamic Acid

bcAlerts.topicZh: 创伤中心转运标准：范围提醒
bcAlerts.bookEn: Describes Accreditation Canada's Level I-V trauma-centre system and the CDC-adapted 4-step field-triage decision tree as the general Canadian destination framework.
bcAlerts.bookZh: 描述了加拿大医疗机构认证局的创伤中心 I-V 分级系统，以及 CDC 改编版四步现场分诊决策树，作为加拿大通用的转运目的地框架。
bcAlerts.bcEn: The BC provincial exam guideline document does not publish its own numeric trauma-centre-level destination criteria — real-world routing follows regional BCEHS dispatch/destination protocols, and the practical exam instead tests the p.7-8 unstable-patient list to decide transport urgency, not which hospital level to choose. Know the Level I-V concept for the written exam, but do not try to memorize a BC-specific numeric version that the guideline does not state.
bcAlerts.bcZh: BC 省级考纲文件没有单独发布自己的创伤中心分级转运数字标准——现实中的转运走 BCEHS 区域调度/目的地协议，而实操考用的是 p.7-8 的不稳定病人清单来决定转运紧急度，而不是选哪一级医院。笔试知道 I-V 级的概念即可，不要去背一套考纲里根本没写的「BC 专属数字版」。
bcAlerts.ref: BC Guidelines p.7-8 (no separate trauma-centre-level section — scope note, not a numeric conflict)
